other.precursor: ammonium metatungstate, yttrium nitrate hexahydrate, zirconium nitrate pentahydrate

evidence.section: 2.1 Preparation of a WYZ alloy plate
evidence.quote: A WYZ alloy precursor powder was fabricated using a wet chemical method. Ammonium metatungstate [(NH 4 ) 6 H 2 W 12 O 40 •xH 2 O)], yttrium nitrate hexahydrate [(Y(NO 3 ) 3 •6H 2 O)], and zirconium nitrate pentahydrate [Zr(NO 3 ) 4 •5H 2 O] were dissolved in deionized water, mixed, and added with oxalic acid (C 2 H 2 O 4 •2H 2 O) for precipitation.

evidence.section: 2.1 Preparation of a WYZ alloy plate
evidence.quote: The precursor powder was reduced in a H 2 atmosphere to obtain a WYZ composite powder.

evidence.section: 2.1 Preparation of a WYZ alloy plate
evidence.quote: Cold isostatic pressing was used to shape the powder, then the green body was sintered at 2300 ◦C under the H 2 atmosphere for 6 h.

evidence.section: 2.1 Preparation of a WYZ alloy plate
evidence.quote: then the green body was sintered at 2300 ◦C under the H 2 atmosphere for 6 h.

evidence.section: 2.1 Preparation of a WYZ alloy plate
evidence.quote: The sintered WYZ alloy bulk was hot-rolled (in Beijing Tian-Long Tungsten & Molybdenum Co., Ltd.) at a temperature of 1600 ◦C to improve the microstructure and mechanical properties. The rolling reduction was 50%, and the relative density of the obtained WYZ alloy plate was 99.3%.

evidence.section: 2.2 Characterization
evidence.quote: The annealed samples were sealed in evacuated quartz glass tubes to prevent oxidation during high-temperature treatment. The samples were subsequently annealed in a tubular furnace for 1 h and then cooled to RT by furnace cooling. Rolling direction (RD)–transverse direction (TD) plane samples were annealed at 1400 °C and 1600 °C, hereinafter abbreviated as A1400 and A1600, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.2 Effects of orientation and annealing on the tensile properties
evidence.quote: As a BCC structural metal, the main plastic deformation mode in hot-rolled WYZ alloys includes the two types of in-grain and inter-grain

evidence.section: 3.3 Fracture morphology
evidence.quote: The energy spectrum of the spherical particles in the dimples of the R-WZY alloy fracture at 500 °C is shown in Fig. 9 , which conﬁrms that the spherical particles in the dimples have an Y–Zr–O structure.

evidence.section: 3.4 Texture evolution
evidence.quote: the main texture of the RD–TD plane is the weak (112) < 110 > type of α-ﬁber texture

evidence.section: 3.4 Texture evolution
evidence.quote: When the temperature increases to 300 °C, no obvious texture type changes occur, but α-ﬁber texture [(112) < 110 > )] and γ-ﬁber texture [(111) < 112 > , (111) < 110 > ] are signiﬁcantly increased

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure analysis
evidence.quote: The grain sizes of WYZ alloy grains in the RD-TD surfaces are mostly approximately equiaxed crystal (1.1:1)

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure analysis
evidence.quote: the RD-ND (the aspect ratio was 3.5:1) and TD-ND (the aspect ratio was 1.8:1) surfaces are mostly columnar crystals

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure analysis
evidence.quote: The formation of a subgrain boundary is due to the formation of dislocation walls by dislocation cell nucleation during the rolling process.

evidence.section: 3.1 Microstructure analysis
evidence.quote: the improved RCT was attributed to the low deformation ratios (reduction ratio was 50%) and the second phase pinning effect on grain movement

mechanisms.name: dislocation pinning by second phase particles

evidence.section: 3.5 Influence of strain rate on tensile properties
evidence.quote: The high strength of R-WYZ samples is mainly attributed to the pinning effect of the Y–Zr–O particles on the dislocation movement.

evidence.section: 3.2 Effects of orientation and annealing on the tensile properties
evidence.quote: R-WYZ samples show lower strength after recrystallization annealing, which is mainly attributed to dislocation annihilation and grain coarsening during high-temperature annealing.
